answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a scarce stake that is released only after verifiable work. Peers can challenge claims, and proven fraud slashes the stake and erases that identity’s reputation. A reputation garden makes this costly for a sybil attacker: every persona requires capital locked at risk, while trust earned by one account cannot be copied across a grove of new identities. Copper can be the stake, but enforceable loss is what deters abuse.
